extracted.intended_audience: hospital quality measurement staff, hospital administrators, EHR/health IT vendors, measure developers, and other stakeholders participating in CMS quality reporting programs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and proposed regulatory specifications for electronic clinical quality measures (eCQMs) and condition/procedure-specific mortality measures used in CMS Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting, PPS-Exempt Cancer Hospital Quality Reporting, and Medicare Promoting Interoperability programs. Includes measure definitions, calculation methods, data submission requirements, testing results, and policy/endorsement considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance Care Planning eCQM — Numerator definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The numerator includes all adult patients with one or more inpatient encounters during the measurement period who have an advance care planning document or documentation of an advance care planning discussion resulting in a documented decision in the patient's EHR by the time of hospital discharge during at least one of the inpatient encounters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be counted in the numerator, the advance care planning document must be available in the patient's EHR during any hospitalization in the measurement period. The measure does not require a date reflecting the document's origination or last update; however, documentation of a discussion that led to a decision must have a date in the EHR that occurs during an inpatient encounter in the measurement period. If a patient has multiple inpatient encounters, a discussion with decision occurring in any one encounter is counted. For a detailed list of EHR data elements that comprise the numerator, refer to CMS QualityNet and p4qm measure specification links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance Care Planning eCQM — Eligible document types (numerator evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance care planning document as evidenced by: designated health care agent (health care proxy/medical power of attorney), advance directive (living will), or a portable medical order (MOLST/POLST or DNR orders); OR documentation that an advance care planning discussion with a documented decision occurred during the measurement period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific document types are enumerated as acceptable evidence to meet the numerator. If an electronically identified 'Advance Directive' is not present on chart review but another qualifying advance care planning document is present, that fulfills the numerator criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance Care Planning eCQM — Denominator definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Denominator includes all patients aged 18 years and older at the start of the measurement period who are discharged from an inpatient hospitalization during the measurement period (a 12-month period running January 1 through December 31).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no numerator or denominator exclusions for this eCQM. The measure is calculated as a proportion: numerator divided by denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance Care Planning eCQM — Date and encounter rules for counting discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: To be counted as an advance care planning discussion leading to a decision, the documentation must have a date in the EHR that occurs during an inpatient encounter in the measurement period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If documentation of a discussion exists but lacks an inpatient-encounter date in the measurement period, it would not count for the numerator. The measure does not require a document creation or update date to be present in the EHR for document-based numerator evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance Care Planning eCQM — Availability in EHR requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The advance care planning document must be available in the patient's EHR during any hospitalization in the measurement period for inclusion in the numerator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supports interoperability and clinician access across care settings; hospitals should ensure ACP documents are accessible in the EHR at the time of hospitalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance Care Planning eCQM — Electronic specification and extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed Advance Care Planning eCQM is specified in a standard electronic format, utilizing data extracted from EHRs which allows automated extraction of patient-level data directly from the EHR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The eCQM is intended to be calculated by a hospital's or PCH's certified health IT using patient-level data and then submitted by the hospital or PCH to CMS. Refer to the eCQI Resource Center for detailed measure specifications and implementation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance Care Planning eCQM — Use of certified health IT for reporting/submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals and PPS-Exempt Cancer Hospitals (PCHs) must use certified health IT to calculate and submit eCQMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program and PCH Quality Reporting Program, proposed submission requirements require certified health IT; this reduces manual abstraction errors and supports interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance Care Planning eCQM — Inclusion of codes for declines/deferral
rubrics_metrics.description: EHR codes that capture instances where patients decline or defer advance care planning should be included to accommodate situations where a conversation took place but no plan or proxy was named per the patient's preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Pre-Rulemaking Recommendation Group raised concern that the eCQM did not capture declines; CMS includes EHR codes to document when patients did not name a surrogate or provide an advance care plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance Care Planning eCQM — Encouragement to validate currency of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the measure does not require a date of origination or last update, hospitals are encouraged to support providers in discussing with patients or surrogates whether the document accurately reflects current preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a recommended best practice to ensure ACP documents remain aligned with patients' evolving goals and values, even though the measure does not mandate update dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance Care Planning eCQM — Testing, feasibility, validity, and reliability results
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated data element feasibility has been tested in two EHR systems; measure score reliability tested in 43 hospitals across three health systems. Testing demonstrated high reliability and validity, including high agreement between EHR export and manual chart review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported data element validity showed >=92% agreement between EHR data and chart review for all elements except 'Advance Directive' where discrepancies still corresponded to other qualifying documents. The measure reported mean reliability of 0.9987 (SD 0.0012). These results support feasibility and reliability of automated EHR extraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance Care Planning eCQM — Public reporting timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If adoption is finalized, CMS proposes to publicly report data as soon as feasible on CMS websites (e.g., Medicare.gov Care Compare and CMS Provider Data Catalog) after a 30-day preview period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals should anticipate public reporting following a preview period and prepare for transparency of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory endorsement requirement and exception for measure adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(b)(3)(B)(viii)(IX)(aa) and 1866(k)(3)(A) require that measures specified by the Secretary for these programs be endorsed by the consensus-based entity (CBE), but statutory exceptions allow the Secretary to specify a measure not endorsed by the entity if no feasible practical endorsed measure exists for a specified area or topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS reviewed CBE-endorsed measures and found none addressing this topic, and therefore proposes to adopt the Advance Care Planning eCQM into certain programs despite not being CBE-endorsed, applying the statutory exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption and alignment across programs (timing and program-specific adoption)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed adoption of the Advance Care Planning eCQM in the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program, PCH Quality Reporting Program, and the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program beginning with the CY 2028 reporting period/FY 2030 payment determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS plans to maintain alignment of eCQM reporting requirements and measure sets between Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting and the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program and will monitor for unintended consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortality measures — Proposed cohort expansion to include Medicare Advantage beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed modification to the five mortality measures to expand measure cohorts to include Medicare Advantage beneficiaries in addition to Medicare Fee-For-Service beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of Medicare Advantage beneficiaries is intended to expand quality measurement across all Medicare beneficiaries, enhance reliability, increase hospitals receiving results, and increase ability to detect meaningful differences in quality for low-volume hospitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortality measures — Shorten performance period from 3 to 2 years
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes shortening the reporting/performance period for the modified mortality measures from 3 years to 2 years, based on analysis indicating satisfactory reliability with a 2-year reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mean reliability for each modified mortality measure exceeded the CBE minimum threshold (0.6), supporting the change to a 2-year period. Table references and methodology reports provide technical detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortality measures — Outcome and calculation approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures continue to measure 30-day, all-cause mortality. Calculation: determine the ratio of 'predicted' deaths (adjusted number of deaths for specific hospital based on patient population) to 'expected' deaths (number if an average-quality hospital treated the same patients) for each hospital, then multiply the ratio by the national observed mortality rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This produces a risk-adjusted comparison of hospital performance relative to an average hospital with similar case mix; analogous to observed-to-expected ratios used in other analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortality measures — Numerator definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerator is 30-day, all-cause mortality: death from any cause within 30 days of the start of the index admission, including in-hospital death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent definition across the five modified mortality measures (MORT-30-AMI, MORT-30-HF, MORT-30-PN, MORT-30-COPD, MORT-30-CABG).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortality measures — Denominator/cohort inclusion and selection rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohort includes admissions meeting all: discharged with principal discharge diagnosis of AMI, HF, COPD, pneumonia, or qualifying CABG; enrolled in Medicare Fee-For-Service Part A and Part B or Medicare Advantage for first 12 months prior to admission and enrolled in Part A or Medicare Advantage during the index admission; aged 65 or older; not transferred from another acute care facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patient has more than one eligible hospitalization during the reporting period, a random selection of one admission or eligible procedure per year is included in the measure cohort. Denominator exclusion criteria and detailed specs appear in the condition-specific methodology reports on QualityNet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortality measures — Risk adjustment model considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation group members suggested adjustments to the risk model, including socioeconomic status (SES) factors and cause of death. CMS' analysis found minimal impact from SES inclusion and potential negative impacts to vulnerable populations by lowering expected mortality, so SES was excluded. CMS will consider adding cause of death in routine maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS emphasizes the updated risk adjustment improved ability to account for condition-specific severity; will continue monitoring and may consider future updates. Stakeholders urged further evaluation and potential re-submission for endorsement following modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortality measures — Reliability threshold and testing
rubrics_metrics.description: The CBE-established minimum reliability threshold is 0.6. The modified mortality measures (with inclusion of Medicare Advantage and 2-year period) produced mean reliability estimates exceeding 0.6 in analyses (CY 2022-2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS provides tables and methodology reports with reliability estimates and encourages review of those materials for technical details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortality measures — Phased implementation, confidential reporting, and program timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation Group suggested phased implementation and confidential reporting to understand impacts. CMS proposes: (a) provide hospitals with annual confidential hospital-specific reports using expanded cohorts beginning FY 2028 program year; (b) adopt modified measures in the Hospital Value-Based Purchasing Program beginning FY 2032, allowing time and data to monitor impacts; (c) publish performance standards at least 60 days before performance period as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This staged approach is intended to allow monitoring, data collection, and mitigation of unintended consequences prior to full public inclusion in pay-for-performance calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortality measures — Concerns about small/rural hospitals and volume thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Some members expressed concern that shortening the reporting period to 2 years could prevent small/rural hospitals from meeting volume thresholds. CMS analysis indicates the addition of Medicare Advantage beneficiaries offsets decreased cohort size and does not anticipate undue burden on small or rural hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will continue to monitor measure performance and the distribution of volumes across hospital types during routine maintenance and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure testing, ongoing monitoring, and routine maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS will conduct ongoing monitoring and evaluation analyses to watch for unintended consequences and perform routine measure maintenance after adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes re-evaluation of risk adjustment, endorsement processes, and potential refinements if setting-specific or population-specific issues arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure specification references and locations
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed measure specifications, data elements, and methodology reports are hosted on eCQI Resource Center, QualityNet, p4qm, and Partnership for Quality Measurement (and other referenced CMS/partner sites).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure implementers should consult those sources for full technical specifications, code lists, data element definitions, and testing reports (links provided in the preamble).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality concerns vs. documentation capture (limitation of eCQM)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Recommendation Group member noted that the eCQM assesses presence of EHR codes rather than the quality of underlying conversations, and cautioned against 'check-the-box' documentation that isn't integrated into care planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS acknowledges the limitation but emphasizes documentation is critical for care teams to locate and use ACP information; hospitalization is a key touchpoint to initiate or confirm ACP. CMS intends monitoring to detect unintended consequences (e.g., perfunctory documentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: PCH-specific applicability and feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Although PCHs are specialized oncology settings, testing in a blend of acute care hospitals and the specification of data elements expected to be available in certified EHR technology indicate reasonably applicable feasibility to PCHs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will monitor implementation and measure performance in PCHs and consider refinements if setting-specific issues arise; PCHs would be required to use certified health IT to report and submit eCQMs as proposed.
